relationships.description: The Defender was distributed across the South by Pullman porters, the workforce the BSCP organized from 1925.
relationships.evidence: BlackPast documents porter distribution of the Defender; labor histories document the BSCP's 1925 founding to organize those porters. [Red-team: no dated direct institutional link cited; synthesis of two separate facts.]

relationships.description: BSCP members worked as porters on Pullman cars running over railroads including the Illinois Central's Chicago-New Orleans mainline.
relationships.evidence: Pullman porters staffed Pullman sleeping cars across railroads; the IC was a major Chicago-New Orleans passenger carrier (American-Rails.com). The specific BSCP-on-IC assignment pattern is inferred, not directly sourced.

relationships.description: The Illinois Central's Central Station terminus funneled Mississippi, Tennessee, and Louisiana migrants into Chicago's South Side.
relationships.evidence: American-Rails.com documents the IC routes and Chicago Central Station; migrant settlement in Bronzeville is documented per-family (see GBL-A-039).
